nodes.title: Register and sign in
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Hashed passwords, cookie sessions, ~/.local/share/openchq or OPENCHQ_WEB_DATA.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Online lobby
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Signed-in sockets see who is online.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Bot room
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Play a bot opens one room. The player sits on the chosen side. The other seat is Bot.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Human room
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Invite, decline, and accept. Accept opens one room with two human seats.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Shared clock flag
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Hold and Run are visible to every seat in the room. Pieces do not move yet.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Lock the scaffold with WEB_OK
nodes.work: Add web/test/run.mjs. It starts the server on 127.0.0.1 with a temporary OPENCHQ_WEB_DATA and a free port. It must not use port 8787. It registers two users, rejects a short password, rejects a wrong password, rejects a duplicate name, opens a bot room, runs and holds the clock, leaves, invites, declines, accepts, and sees the room end when the other socket closes. A socket with no cookie gets HTTP 401. The process prints WEB_OK and exits 0. It kills only the server it started.
nodes.prove: node web/test/run.mjs prints WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Terrain and sites on the server
nodes.work: Read the extract the way the desktop archive did: OPENCHQ_DATA, then local/data_root.txt, then data/. Load data/tmap.bin as 320 by 136 nibbles with row stride 162, and data/sites.json. GET /api/board returns width, height, cell ids, and sites. Washington and Moscow are the capitals. The JSON has no image bytes and no path to WORLD_MAP.png, the stills, or the unpacked executable.
nodes.prove: The harness requests /api/board and requires 320 by 136, both capitals, and no forbidden payload. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Paint the cell grid in the page
nodes.work: The match canvas draws cell ids from /api/board. Ocean, shallows, land, city, and capital are distinct colors. The schematic remains only when the extract is missing, and the page says the extract is missing. Do not draw the original picture.
nodes.prove: A pure painter test checks the color of ocean, shallows, city, and capital. The harness still prints WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Rooms outlive the process
nodes.work: A room is a row, not a Map entry. web/server/rooms.mjs owns a rooms table on the same SQLite database; the lobby writes on create and on every clock change, deletes only on a real end, and restores every stored room paused at boot. Idle rooms older than 24 hours are pruned. A restart never resumes a clock.
nodes.prove: The harness starts a bot room, runs the clock, kills the server, restarts it on the same data directory and reconnects: the same room id comes back, held, with the caller still in its seat. Removing the store write makes that assertion fail.
nodes.evidence: Committed with the storage pass; WEB_OK with the restart block in web/test/run.mjs.

nodes.title: Timing and prices live in one file
nodes.work: config/game.json holds every player-facing number: round length, pay cadence, starting pool, prices, fuel reserve and burn, sight radius, enemy route steps, HITS. web/server/rules.mjs loads it once per process and exposes roundSeconds(), payEvery(), priceOf(), landPace(), seaAccepts(), sightCells(), enemyRouteSteps(), startPool(). No module may hard-code a round length, a price, a sight radius or a terrain cost.
nodes.prove: The harness imports rules.mjs and asserts the loaded values match config/game.json, that landPace refuses wasteland and charges slow ground, and that the server reports the configured round length. Changing config/game.json changes the reported value without touching code.
nodes.evidence: Round length set to 5 s by the owner on 2026-11-06: at 1 cell per round the Washington-Moscow march is ~104 cells, about 8.7 minutes, where 0.14 s made a 24-second war.

nodes.title: Opening pieces
nodes.work: A match module in JavaScript places Blue at Washington and Red at Moscow, plus one ship each, for 1918, 1942, 1986, and the concealed era. 2023 places no pieces. Creating a bot or human room attaches this match. The room view includes the caller's pieces.
nodes.prove: The harness opens a 1986 bot room and sees four pieces, then a 2023 bot room and sees none. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Server tick
nodes.work: The server advances a running room one round at a time. Tests call the tick function directly and do not sleep. A held clock does not move pieces. One running round is the same 0.14 second live interval, and tests do not wait that interval.
nodes.prove: The harness holds a room for five direct ticks and sees no movement, then runs it for one tick. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Land orders
nodes.work: A seat orders its own land piece to a cell. The piece walks one cell per running round. X wraps. Y does not. Wasteland is refused. Ocean and lake are transport. Forest, mountain, polar, jungle, and shallows take longer than open ground. The pace ratio stays unnamed.
nodes.prove: The harness orders the Blue army one open step and sees that cell after one running tick. A wasteland order is refused. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Sea lanes
nodes.work: Ships move on the lane graph. The server may read the unpacked executable on the machine that hosts the server and cache waypoints it computed. The browser never receives that file. A land piece ordered from sea to sea follows the lanes. A land-to-land order stays on land.
nodes.prove: The harness sails the Blue ship one lane step and checks the land-to-land order did not become a sea route. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Bot seat
nodes.work: In a bot room the empty seat marches its army toward the player's capital and sails its ship once when the path is empty. It does not repath the ship every round.
nodes.prove: The harness runs a bot room and sees the bot army take a path toward the player capital and the bot ship take one path. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Two human seats
nodes.work: In a human room neither seat is given bot orders. Each socket may order only its own side. A forged side is refused.
nodes.prove: The harness accepts an invite, orders each side, and proves a forged side does not move the other army. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Stop short and fight
nodes.work: Two pieces never stop on the same cell. They stop one cell short. A shot happens every other round of one continuous fight. No damage number is stored or shown. Removal waits until a later measured hit count. Do not invent that count in this node.
nodes.prove: The harness places two hostile armies on adjacent cells, ticks, and sees them still on those cells with a shot note that has no digit. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Per-seat view
nodes.work: A seat sees its own pieces, enemy pieces within Chebyshev 8 with X wrapping, and only the first three steps of an enemy route. A still submarine is omitted. In the concealed era the other side is omitted until its capital is found. Hidden pieces are absent from the JSON.
nodes.prove: The harness puts an enemy army 9 cells away and asserts it is missing from the view, then moves it to 8 cells and asserts it is present. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Buying
nodes.work: Land and aircraft buy on a friendly city. Ships buy on a friendly dock. Before the clock has ever run, the purchase does not spend the pool. After the match is running, it spends the stand-in price and marks that city unready with no duration. Infantry is 1 billion. A tank is 2. Ships, submarines, and aircraft are 2. A nuke is refused. Two pieces cannot share a cell.
nodes.prove: The harness buys a tank after the clock has run and sees the pool fall by 2, then sees a nuke refused. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Oil ownership
nodes.work: Wells start with the country they are in. USA is Blue. Russia matches USSR and is Red. Any other named region stays that name. A unit standing on a well captures it. Do not copy production ratings. The well rate stays unknown.
nodes.prove: The harness steps a Blue unit onto a Red well and sees the owner become Blue. The payload does not contain the word production. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Docks and wells must exist as sites
nodes.work: data/sites.json carries only city, capital and facility records. Docks are terrain id 1 (150 painted cells) and wells come from the oil resource list, so a room's site list has no dock for a ship to buy at and no well for a side to hold. Merge docks from the painted terrain and wells from the resource positions onto match.sites at room creation, keeping each record's id, name, x, y and kind, and leave any site whose kind is unknown as it is. Do not invent a production rating for a well.
nodes.prove: The harness opens a 1986 room, counts docks and wells on the match site list, buys a ship at a dock, and captures a well by standing on it. A room created with no extract still opens (empty site list) instead of throwing.

nodes.title: Income into the pool
nodes.work: City income is one billion per city held. Oil income is one billion per well the side holds. On rounds 25, 50, 75, and so on, add both levels to that side's pool. Capitals are not cities. A shortage does not pay. A finished match does not keep paying.
nodes.prove: The harness ticks to round 25 with a known city count and well count and checks the pool. Round 24 does not pay. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Fuel per side
nodes.work: Each side has its own reserve, starting at 10000 and burning 1 on each running round that side has no unit on a well. Zero stops that side only. The other side still moves, buys, and collects income. Standing on any well refills that side's reserve.
nodes.prove: The harness sets Blue's reserve to 1, ticks once, and sees Blue stopped while Red still moves. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Hold both capitals
nodes.work: The match ends when one side owns both capitals. Further ticks do not move pieces, pay income, or burn fuel. The room tells both seats who won.
nodes.prove: The harness gives one side both capitals, ticks, and sees the winner and a frozen board on the next tick. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: A thousand rooms inside one round
nodes.work: Prove the target scale on this host, with numbers, not adjectives. tools/bench-rooms.mjs measures a full tick pass over N rooms and the cost of snapshotting them to the store. Assert in the harness that 1000 rooms of 8 pieces tick and snapshot well inside the 0.14 s round budget, and that a held room costs nothing: no tick, no write. Report the headroom multiples. Do not shrink the model to make the number look good.
nodes.prove: node tools/bench-rooms.mjs 1000 8 reports headroom above 10x for both the tick pass and the snapshot, and the harness prints WEB_OK including that assertion.

nodes.title: Reconnect
nodes.work: A dropped socket does not delete the room or free the seat: the match is held, kept in the store, and reserved for that account, and it does not tick, pay or burn fuel while nobody watches. That pause-and-keep half already ships (done ahead of this node, proved by the harness: drop a seat, the room survives paused, the connected seat can run it again). What remains here: a returning socket gets the same filtered view of its seat it had before (own pieces, sight 8, first three enemy steps), and the absent seat's standing orders are still in the match and still execute when the clock runs.
nodes.prove: The harness closes one socket, connects again as the same user, and sees the same room id and its own pieces. WEB_OK.
nodes.note: pause-on-empty shipped with the room_store pass

nodes.title: Remove the Godot tree from this branch
nodes.work: Delete the Godot project files from the web branch only after every dependency is done and WEB_OK still passes. Do not delete the desktop-godot branch. Do not touch github main.
nodes.prove: The harness still prints WEB_OK. project.godot is gone on this branch. origin/desktop-godot still exists.

nodes.title: Send what changed, not the whole view
nodes.work: A full seat view every round measured at 2.6 MB per round for 2000 seats (~18 MB/s), which is the real cost of 1000 concurrent games. Send per-round deltas: changed pieces, new and cleared route steps, and a periodic full resync. Keep the payload honest - hidden pieces stay absent. Record before and after bytes per round in the harness.
nodes.prove: tools/bench-rooms.mjs and the harness report bytes per round for a 1000-room tick before and after, and the delta payload is at least 5x smaller while a client that missed a delta still gets a correct view after the resync.

nodes.title: More than oil, and still no invented rates
nodes.work: The successor will differ from the 1990 game here on purpose. Add resource kinds as data (config/game.json) with a generic holding + consumption model instead of one-off oil code, keep per-side reserves, and gate each kind by era. Any rate the owner has not set stays unnamed and unplaced rather than guessed. This is an owner-designed expansion, not a recovery of the original.
nodes.prove: The harness asserts a second resource kind can be configured, held, consumed and shown without new code paths per kind, and that an unset rate is refused rather than defaulted to a number.

nodes.title: Make the match length a decision, not a leftover
nodes.work: Measure a real match end to end: rounds to first contact, rounds to a capital, rounds between income payments, and wall-clock minutes at the configured round length. Report the curve. If it is too short or too long, change config/game.json and re-measure; do not tune individual numbers by feel and do not change the rules to make a clock look right.
nodes.prove: A recorded run reports wall-clock minutes for a 1986 bot match and the income cadence in seconds, and the harness asserts the match takes at least the owner's chosen floor (config) before a capital falls.

nodes.title: Decide single instance or many, with numbers
nodes.work: One process holds 2000 sockets and ticks 1000 rooms inside the round budget. Decide whether the product needs more than one instance (uptime, region, load). If yes, the room store moves to Postgres and rooms are sharded per instance with a sticky socket; if no, record that the volume-pinned single instance is the accepted design and what would overturn it.
nodes.prove: A written decision in docs/SCALE.md with the measured numbers it rests on, and the harness still prints WEB_OK on whichever path was chosen.
